newsitem.title: USA: Dow seen up 50 to 80 points at open, Japan calms.
newsitem.headline: Dow seen up 50 to 80 points at open, Japan calms.

text.p: Wall Street was expected to open higher on Tuesday, driven by bargain hunting after Monday's steep sell-off and reassured by Japanese government comments regarding Japan's holdings of U.S. government bonds.
The Standard & Poor's 500 futures index was up eight points at 889.75 and the long bond rose 8/32 to 6.69 percent.

"The market could open up 50 to 80 points higher, though that's a guess because programs will kick in," Ron Doran, director of institutional trading at C.L. King and Associates, said. "A lot of yesterday's sell-off was not warranted."
